note.question: What determines innovation sourcing and supplier governance?
note.overview: The innovation-sourcing contest has hidden effort and private performance shocks; suppliers play a Bayesian effort game and the buyer optimizes governance/contract choices around that equilibrium.

components.label: pure-strategy Bayesian Nash effort equilibrium nested in the buyer's governance/contract problem
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is pure-strategy Bayesian Nash effort equilibrium nested in the buyer's governance/contract problem. Equations (1)-(4) on PDF p. 6 nest effort best responses and ex post selection inside the award problem for a given k. Lemma 1 on PDF pp. 6-7 proves that the independent supplier wins iff v_1>v_2+kA, exposing the ownership-induced selection bias. Lemma 2 and Propositions 1-3 on PDF pp. 7-10 solve the ownership case; Lemma 3 and Propositions 4-5 on PDF pp. 11-14 characterize control, under which the buyer directs only affiliated supplier 2's effort.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Without control, the two suppliers simultaneously choose hidden innovation effort; supplier-specific private shocks then determine submitted product performance, which the buyer evaluates before selecting the winner. Under control, the buyer directly chooses affiliated supplier 2's effort while independent supplier 1 chooses its own effort. Bayesian innovation contest hidden-action supplier game
